title: Symmetric cuts in an 80° isosceles triangle
statement: In isosceles △ABC, AB=AC and ∠A=80°. D∈BC, E∈CA, F∈AB satisfy CE=CD and BF=BD. Find ∠EDF.
local_hints: The outer 80° isosceles triangle has 50° base angles; use them inside the two smaller isosceles triangles.
Recall GEO-ISO-01 · Turn equal lengths into equal angles.

title: Two isosceles triangles with perpendicular equal sides
statement: Triangles ABC and ABD satisfy AB=AC=BD. Lines AC and BD intersect and are perpendicular. Find ∠ACB+∠ADB.
local_hints: Each triangle is isosceles, so only two base-angle variables are needed.
Recall GEO-ISO-01 and the 90° direction relation from GEO-RIGHT-01.

title: An equilateral triangle inside an isosceles triangle
statement: In isosceles △ABC, AB=AC. Points D∈AB, E∈BC, F∈CA form equilateral △DEF. Prove ∠DEB=½(∠ADF+∠CFE).
local_hints: Use one outer base-angle variable; every angle inside the equilateral triangle is 60°.
Recall GEO-ISO-01 · Turn equal lengths into equal angles.

title: Intersection of two perpendicular bisectors
statement: D,E are midpoints of AB,AC. The line through D perpendicular to AB and the line through E perpendicular to AC meet at O. Prove OA=OB=OC.
local_hints: “Midpoint + perpendicular” is exactly a perpendicular bisector.

title: Perpendicular bisecting diagonals
statement: Segments AB and CD bisect each other at right angles. Prove quadrilateral ACBD has all four sides equal.
local_hints: At the diagonal intersection you have equal half-diagonals and four right angles.

title: Crossed equal sides force congruence
statement: Triangles ABC and DBC lie on the same base BC and same side. BA=CD and BD=CA. Lines AC and BD meet at O. Prove △OBA≅△OCD.
local_hints: Prove a larger triangle pair congruent before attacking the small triangles at O.
Recall GEO-CONG-01 · Choose the congruent pair that reveals the target.

title: A bisected angle in a parallelogram
statement: In parallelogram ABCD, diagonal AC bisects ∠DAB. Prove ABCD is a rhombus.
local_hints: The angle bisector and the parallel opposite side manufacture equal angles in triangle ACD.

title: Constructing a parallel segment equal to a remainder
statement: Given △ABC, construct D∈AB and E∈AC such that DE∥BC and DE=BD.
local_hints: DE∥BC guarantees similarity, so turn DE=BD into a ratio on AB before constructing.
answer: Construct D with AD:DB=AB:BC, then draw DE∥BC

title: Four parallelograms around an arbitrary point
statement: ABCD is a parallelogram and O any point. Complete parallelograms OAEB, OBFC, OCGD, ODHA. Prove EFGH is a parallelogram.
local_hints: Every new fourth vertex of a parallelogram is a linear combination of the old vertices.
Recall GEO-VECTOR-01 · Use vectors for repeated parallelograms.

title: Equal perpendicular distances from endpoints of a bisected segment
statement: C is the midpoint of AB and line ℓ passes through C. Perpendiculars AD⊥ℓ and BE⊥ℓ meet ℓ at D,E. Prove AD=BE.
local_hints: A 180° rotation about the midpoint C swaps A and B while leaving the line through C invariant.

title: Points equidistant from two intersecting lines
statement: Lines AB and CD intersect at O. Another line XY is given. Show that, in general, two points on XY are equidistant from AB and CD. Determine when there is only one such point.
local_hints: This is a locus question: points equidistant from two intersecting lines lie on their angle bisectors.
Recall GEO-LOCUS-01 · Translate equidistance into a locus.
answer: Intersections of XY with the two angle bisectors; exactly one when XY is parallel to one bisector but not coincident

title: Symmetric extensions of an isosceles base
statement: ABC is isosceles with AB=AC. Extend BC beyond B to D and beyond C to E so that BD=CE. Prove AD=AE.
local_hints: Compare the two outer triangles created by the equal base extensions.

title: A right triangle with hypotenuse twice a leg
statement: In right △ABC, AC is the hypotenuse and AC=2AB. Prove ∠BAC=2∠ACB.
local_hints: Hypotenuse twice one leg is the 30-60-90 trigger.
